item.title: Legal Matrix 2026 — Norm, Actor, Trigger, Remedy
item.lead: The legal analysis can be even more precise by linking every possible norm violation to an actor and a piece of evidence.

blocks.text: In consumer law, the central question revolves around misleading actions or omissions and their impact on the economic behavior of the consumer. The UCPD Guidance explicitly addresses online platforms, personalization, dark patterns, and influencer marketing.

In privacy, the focus is on purpose, legal basis, proportionality, transparency, data minimization, and any special categories. EDPB material emphasizes that Article 9 can also affect relevant derived/inferred data.

In the DSA, this includes dark patterns, transparency, and recommender systems. Under AI Act Article 50, the focus is on the transparency of certain AI interactions and content. The new edition prevents one law from having to solve all problems.

blocks.label: LEGAL IMPROVEMENT
blocks.text: The question “which law fails?” is replaced by “which obligation covers which fact, and what remains as a residual category?”

blocks.label: UCPD
blocks.text: Misleading representation of who is communicating Interface + terms and conditions + chat log

blocks.label: GDPR
blocks.text: Processing / profiling of personal data Privacy notice + data fields + logs

blocks.label: DSA
blocks.text: Manipulative interface / recommender UX test + recommender info

rows: Unfair or disproportionate terms and conditions
